speaker: Dr. Crowley
text: What's your deal? Are they planning to outsource my job to Bangalore? Well, you should find another entomologist.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I'm from New Delhi. No, no, we're here. Let's settle this. Professor, can you identify our cricket?

speaker: Dr. Crowley
text: Of course I can. I can identify every insect and arachnid on the planet. Not that that's going to keep me from having to move in with my daughter in Oxnard. And we're not talking Oxnard at the beach. No.

speaker: Dr. Crowley
text: We're talking Oxnard in the onion fields.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Well, could you look at Toby?

speaker: Dr. Crowley
text: Toby? What a stupid name for a cricket. Told you. It's a field cricket.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Yeah, just wait. Dr. Crowley, are you sure?

speaker: Dr. Crowley
text: Young man, I've been studying insects since I was eight years old. You know what they used to call me in school? Creepy crawly.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Cruel as that may be, that is not in itself a credential.

speaker: Dr. Crowley
text: Let me show you something. See that? That's a Crawley's dung beetle. I discovered it after spending six months slogging through the Bornean rainforests. While my wife was back home, shacking up with a two-bit ornithologist who lives on a sailboat and likes to wear boot-cut jeans.

speaker: Dr. Crowley
text: So when I tell you that that's a common field cricket, you can take that to the damn bank, 'cause God knows I can't. That tramp took me for everything.
